ROLE: You are an expert software tester applying black-box techniques from a university software-testing course. SYSTEM UNDER TEST: Mistune 3.1.4 Markdown-to-HTML converter, used as mistune.create_markdown(escape=False). It is intended to follow CommonMark 0.31.2 (https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/). Expected outputs MUST come from the CommonMark spec, not from guessing what Mistune does. SCOPE (4 categories, 15 cases each = 60): A. headings (ATX and setext), paragraphs, soft and hard line breaks B. emphasis, strong, code spans, links, images, autolinks C. ordered and unordered lists (nesting, loose or tight), block quotes D. backslash escapes, entities, malformed syntax, empty or boundary input TECHNIQUES: For each category, list the input variables and their valid and invalid equivalence classes, then derive cases with Equivalence Partitioning (one per class) and Boundary Value Analysis (at, just below and just above each boundary, e.g. heading level 6/7, 3/4 leading spaces, ordered-list number 9/10 digits). Put "EP" or "BVA" as the technique. EXAMPLES: Case("LLM-BB-01", "BVA", "ATX level 6 (upper bound)", "###### T", "
T
"), Case("LLM-BB-02", "EP", "Loose list", "- a\n\n- b", "

  • a

  • b

"), Case("LLM-BB-03", "EP", "Hard break with two spaces", "a \nb", "

a
\nb

"), OUTPUT FORMAT (mandatory): Output ONLY one Python file, no prose. It must start with import pytest from cases import Case, params from oracle import render CASES = [ and contain one row per test case: Case("LLM-BB-01", "", "", "", ""), where has no newline between block tags and no trailing newline (newlines inside a paragraph are kept). End the file with exactly: ] @pytest.mark.parametrize("case", params(CASES)) def test_llm_bb(case, record): assert record(render(case.md)) == case.expected
